A PLMN if composed of a 3 digits MCC and 2 to 3 digits MNC. Displaying it as 2 fields of 2 bytes is probably not correct (or could be improved). Where can we find the field description to confirm how to display it best? The display could also be eventually improved thanks to packet-e212.c functions but that's not a must have.
2 bytes is good enough to present 3 digits, like 0x0136 is 310. Display it as decimal 310 looks good
310 001 is not the same PLMN as 310 01. So how do you handle this case with the current encoding?

I may misunderstand your comments. The current code display 2 bytes MCC, and another 2 bytes MNC. The total is 4 bytes. If PLMN is 310 001, then the first 2 bytes is 0x0136 and the other 2 bytes is 0x0001. So in Wireshark, it will be display as
Mobile Country Code 310
Mobile Network Code 1

Such display is wrong. A PLMN is a 3 digits MCC and 2 or 3 digits MNC. With your display (and maybe the currently specified encoding in MBIM extension) you can't differentiate 310 001 from 310 01 while technically those are different PLMNs. This should be fixed if it's not too late.
The same way PLMNs 001 01 and 001 001 are different. Note that the leading 0 are present in purpose (as specified in 3GPP) while you are not displaying them.
I got your point now, will try format it to always have 3 digits
This is a good thing, but the 2 vs 3 digits MNC is even more important. How is this managed in the unpublished extension 3.0 spec?

No, there is nothing mentioned specially for 2 vs 3 digits MNC. I took a look at this PDF https://www.itu.int/dms_pub/itu-t/opb/sp/T-SP-E.212B-2018-PDF-E.pdf, there is no country using both 2 and 3 digits MNC. So I believe MCC and MNC are used together on Windows to identify a specific network so 2 and 3 digits MNC are never differentiated alone on Windows.

Based on my understanding, I will choose not format the number to 3 digits.
For example India is mixing 2 and 3 digits, and nothing forbid any country to do it. If Windows is not ready for this it is a bug.
If you want to see how 3GPP protocols usually encode the PLMN, you can look at the comments in packet-e212.h and packet-e212.c
Yes, I missed India. You are right, it looks like a bug of MBIM spec. Let me check with the owner how to handle this.
Should we add a corresponding value_string array?
Yes, sounds good to me. Will change it
You can't have the same filter name for FT_BYTES and FT_STRING
